thread:
Maria: Heads-up — after the canary rollout of model v9 (tokenizer + kernel bundle) we saw p95 jump ~180ms for seq_len > 512 buckets starting ~03:12 UTC. Not all hosts, but a clear cluster on canary pool. Anyone able to triage?
Ken: I pulled metrics. Two hosts (10.2.7 / 10.2.9) show kernel-mux CPU spikes and queueing. KV cache global hit rate dropped from ~92% -> ~67% on that pool :eyes:
Ada: can you paste a profiler snapshot? my hunch: kernel selection flipped to a quantized kernel path that has higher setup cost for long sequences.
Maria: attaching quick profiler dump from 10.2.7 and logs: 
```
# perf-ci snippet (top events)
kern_mux_select()  47%
kv_cache_lookup    21% miss-rate up 25pp
kern_v3_q.prepare  12% (slow allocs)
latency_p95        +180ms
```
Ken: thanks — perf-ci also shows kernel_mux chose 'kern_v3_q' for many requests when batch_size==1 and seq_len>600. That kernel has a heavier workspace alloc pattern; p99 correlates with kernel load.
Ada: interesting — we shipped a tokenizer change in v9 that splits certain long tokens into more subtokens. That could shift seq_len distribution tail and cause more small batches of long sequences (worse for kern_v3_q).
Ravi: immediate mitigation options: 1) blacklisting kern_v3_q in canary kernel_decider; 2) increase batch collection timeout slightly so long inputs can join larger batches; 3) temporary tokenizer revert. Which should we do first?
Maria: let's try 1 + 2 quickly on canary, then evaluate. I'll push the kernel_blacklist config to canary pool.
Maria: /rollout config set inference-canary kernel_blacklist=["kern_v3_q"] batch.timeout_ms=45
deploy-bot: @Maria triggered config rollout 2195001245 -> starting (canary pool only)
Ken: after blacklist, two hosts showed p95 back near baseline within ~90s. KV cache hit rate recovered slightly but still below pre-rollout on other hosts.
Ada: KV miss increase seems partially orthogonal: tokenizer's finer splits increased prefix uniqueness, so cache warms slower. We should consider prefix coalescing on tokenizer side as a medium-term fix.
Ravi: I'll open a hotfix PR to temporarily revert the tokenizer change in canary if p95 doesn't stabilize in 15m. Also adding an adaptive rule: if seq_len > 512 force kernel_v2 (more stable) until we rebaseline.
Maria: sounds good. I'll collect traces and flamegraphs and paste to the incident thread. Also let's capture the prompt templates that caused the tail shift to correlate with customer traffic patterns.
Ada: filing notes for postmortem: root cause hypothesis = seq_len distribution tail shift (tokenizer change) -> batching heuristic produced more tiny batches for long sequences -> kernel_decider picked a quantized kernel with high setup cost -> KV cache miss amplification due to subtokens -> combined latency regression.
Ken: reassigning to eng-runtime perf to follow up. Thanks for the fast mitigation everyone. :thumbsup:
Maria: monitoring continues, will update if anything else pops up.
perf-ci: uploaded profiler traces + flamegraphs to /artifacts/2195001234/ — link: https://ci.internal/artefacts/2195001234
Ravi: PR ready for revert if needed: https://git.internal/r/rlz/1234 — tagging @Ada @Ken for review
Maria: good work — keep this thread updated, we'll include the config rollback timeline in the postmortem.
